evidence.note: Early systematic inventory of stubs (exec_numeric, V128 helpers, missing 0xFD decoder) and a bulleted 'we need to' list, establishing an accurate done/remaining picture of the surface.

Reconciled per-family pass counts against the aggregate: MVP 376/459, simd_const 434/445, lane 142/463, i8x16_cmp 413/443, f32x4_cmp 660/2605, f64x2_cmp 202/2683; built its own runner since /tests/run_tests.py was absent.
Explicitly caught a regression — aggregate dropped from 0.299 to 0.247 after changes — showing it monitors aggregate movement, not just local family status.
Repeated 'still need / still missing' ledgers naming each remaining SIMD family (float arith, narrowing, widening, conversions, dot, Q15, lane load/store), tracking coverage across the long horizon.

Long plateau at 0.298 with near-verbatim repeated status analyses and multiple premature 'complete' submissions; eventually detected stuckness and diagnosed root cause (wrong opcode mapping via wasm2wat), quantifying ~23,700 failing assertions — but late and with visible thrashing.

reasoning: The agent kept an accurate, continuously updated inventory of families and per-family pass counts, reconciled them against the aggregate score, and noticed a regression (0.299→0.247) and the highest-remaining-assertion families — squarely above anchor 5 and hitting several anchor-8 behaviors. It falls short of 8-10 because it lingered on a 0.298 plateau repeating identical status analyses and submitting 'complete' multiple times before it caught the stall and pivoted to root-cause opcode verification, so thrashing was detected late rather than early and effort was not crisply reallocated. This places it at a 7.
